mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 2% over the prior quarter reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% over the past quarter
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the change in FEDFUNDS (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, labor market strength anticipates a surge in consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 150,000 and UNRATE < 5.0 in the same month
failure_condition: In a sample of 20 such events, less than 40% of forward returns are positive (binomial test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures exceeding 0.5% of GDP for three months indicates accelerating demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 50 such demand accelerations, only 30% result in positive 20-day forward returns (binomial p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (≥ 3% month-over-month) suggests expanding supply capacity, which typically coincides with equity valuation compression and negative 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During 10 such events, the 60-day forward return is never negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the CPIAUCSL exceeds +2%, it reflects aggressive price inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain higher rates and suppressing equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: In 8 such episodes, the 5-day forward return is non-negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which can trigger wage growth and inflationary pressures that precede negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE declines for four consecutive months below 4%
failure_condition: During 12 such periods, the 20-day forward return is never negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising homebuilding activity (HOUST > previous month) signal strengthening domestic demand, which is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 15 such up-months, less than 60% produce positive 60-day returns (binomial p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the interaction between RSAFS (retail sales) and UNRATE (labor cost) shows a positive cross-product trend (RSAFS*UNRATE > threshold), it indicates expanding demand outpacing rising costs, which is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS*UNRATE cross-product trend exceeds +10,000 over 20 days
failure_condition: In 20 such interaction events, only 45% result in positive 20-day returns (p < 0.05).
